messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: installing RStan with dependencies=TRUE
parts:
Is there a way to have this happen automatically? We're
getting users just hearing RStan is on CRAN and typing

> install.packages("rstan")

and breaking their build. I know the instructions say

dependencies=TRUE

but users aren't reading the instructions because they just
expect the first command to work.

Or would there be a way to output a really big warning?

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: installing RStan with dependencies=TRUE
parts:
To be honest, I'm not even sure why we need people to use dependencies=TRUE.

I might be wrong, but I think the only difference between specifying dependencies=TRUE and omitting it is whether "suggested" packages are installed (packages listed under Suggests in the package Description file) and their dependencies also installed, etc. But if we really need people to install one or several of the packages in Suggests then they aren't suggestions but requirements and we should move them to Imports so they are automatically installed.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: installing RStan with dependencies=TRUE
parts:
On Friday, September 18, 2015 at 2:21:43 PM UTC-4, Jonah wrote:
To be honest, I'm not even sure why we need people to use dependencies=TRUE.

StanHeaders, BH, and RcppEigen need to be on the hard disk in order to build models, but they have no R code so there is nothing to import. 2.8.0 has a better error message if rstan gets installed but these three packages cannot be found.

Ben
